The evidence yields a final answer that acknowledges both the scientific conclusion of natural red hair and the practice of dyeing. The query asks whether he dyed his hair red; the scientific sources indicate his hair was naturally red, but also mention dyeing of the mummy's hair or religious dyeing. Therefore, the answer must incorporate both viewpoints.

Pharaoh Ramses II had natural red hair in his youth, as microscopic analysis of his hair roots revealed natural red pigments [d1, d3, d4, d5, d7]. His mummy's hair was dyed reddish-yellow with henna by embalmers [d1], and he may have dyed his hair red in life to express religious belief in God Seth [d6]. Thus, he both had natural red hair and engaged in dyeing practices.
